Retired year = 2018. IGU 2019 World LNG Report (primary-grade, verified: 2018+Bontang+decommissioned all present) states Bontang had 'only four trains remained in operation as of the end of 2018, with two trains assumed to have been decommissioned during the year' and a footnote 'decommissioning of two trains at Bontang LNG, assumed in December 2018.' The four remaining trains from end-2018 are E,F,G,H (confirmed by GIIGNL 2021 which lists E/F/G/H exporting), so the two decommissioned in Dec 2018 were the older C and D (Bontang T3-4, first LNG 1983); the still-older A and B had already gone offline in the early 2010s. The 2018 YEAR is well-sourced (single strong primary source); tier held to LOW because the assignment of the Dec-2018 wave specifically to units C and D (vs A/B) is inferred from train age/commissioning order and the IGU 2020 statement that A/B were the 'decommissioning status' pair -- the IGU text does not name train letters. researcher_notes: Operating start = year crude-oil export operations began at Enterprise's Houston Ship Channel oil terminal. It loaded one of the first post-export-ban US crude cargoes for Vitol (booked Dec 2015, loaded early Jan 2016) — among the first US crude export operations. Single source verified (gCaptain) tying Enterprise + Houston + 2016 to the first crude export; the terminal handled domestic crude before this, but 2016 is the crude-export-operations start. Original commissioning year of the underlying terminal is not documented independently. tier:low (single non-primary source).

2016 = COMMERCIAL START of dedicated marine export operations at the EHT/Morgan's Point complex: Enterprise's own history page states the Morgan's Point ethane export terminal (Houston Ship Channel) was placed into commercial service in Sept 2016 (initial startup 12 Jul 2016 per Argus; first ethane cargo ~1 Sep 2016 on M/V JS INEOS Intrepid per Hart Energy). 3 independent publishers (Enterprise IR/history primary, Argus, Hart Energy). CAVEAT: the underlying Galena Park LPG marine terminal within the EHT complex is older ('since 1980s') but has no citable 4-digit origin year; 2013-2015 dates found are LPG-export capacity EXPANSIONS of an already-operating terminal, not an operating-start; a later ethylene export terminal at Morgan's Point entered service Dec 2020. If GEM's EHT record is scoped to the ethane/ethylene marine export terminal, 2016 is the documented operating-start; if scoped strictly to the 1980s Galena Park LPG terminal, the precise year is unresolved.

Operating start = year crude/condensate export operations commenced at the Seabrook marine terminal (Galveston Bay). An Aug 2018 announcement states export capabilities had 'recently commenced' (initial expansion was due online mid-2018) → 2018. Identity caveat: the terminal is operated by Seabrook Logistics LLC (Magellan Midstream / LBC JV); ExxonMobil is a connected crude shipper/owner, which is presumably why GEM names it 'ExxonMobil Seabrook.' Both verified URLs derive from the same Magellan/LBC press release (one underlying source), so tier:low / independent:false.

2009 = year Flint Hills Resources (Koch) acquired and began operating the Ingleside crude oil marine terminal. FHR's own press release (via PRNewswire) states verbatim: 'Acquired in 2009, the Ingleside terminal is a gateway to global markets...'. Tier medium/independent=false because all other 2009 hits (BIC Magazine, StorageTerminals Magazine, NS Energy, Oil&Gas360) are verbatim republications of this same FHR release = one underlying document. CAVEAT: separate marine-dock/pipeline buildout milestones exist ~2011-2014 (KPL pipeline into Ingleside; dock expansion) and a 2019 storage expansion, but those are not the operations-start. 2009 is the operator-stated year for the terminal.

substatus 'planned' = a PLANNED retirement, so the year is the planned retirement/decommissioning year. In April 2026 Freeport LNG filed with FERC to decommission/demolish its obsolete import-regasification facilities, requesting that the import authorization be terminated by no later than December 31, 2026 → planned retirement year 2026. (The import/regas terminal began operating June 2008 and effectively ceased after its last import cargo in Feb 2011, but the formal retirement is this 2026 decommissioning.) Two independent origins verified: LNG Prime (original trade reporting) and a Reuters-sourced report carried by energynow.com (also corroborated by Industrial Info).

Proposed year for Train 4 (T4). Freeport LNG filed its FERC application and commenced front-end engineering and design (FEED) for the proposed fourth liquefaction train on June 29, 2017 (FERC docket CP17-470; FERC authorization later granted May 2019) → first publicly proposed 2017. Single primary source (sponsor press release) verified, hence medium.

Phillips 66 Freeport LPG Export Terminal (Freeport, TX) declared fully operational in December 2016; first contracted cargo departed on the VLGC 'Commander' on Dec 16, 2016. Year = 2016 (commercial start). Phillips 66 IR is the primary source; OGJ, Hydrocarbon Engineering and Gas Processing & LNG are independent trade-press confirmations. All four verified PASS for '2016'+'Freeport'.

Targa Resources' Galena Park international LPG export terminal (Houston Ship Channel) brought its international LPG export expansion online in two phases: Phase I in 3Q 2013 and Phase II in 3Q 2014. Year = 2013 for the start of large-scale international LPG export service. Only one source (Targa's own Jan-2013 press release) verified PASS for '2013'+'Galena Park' before the session web limit; it announces the project coming online in 3Q2013. CAVEAT: the underlying marine terminal pre-dated 2013, so 2013 is the international-LPG-export online year rather than the terminal's original commissioning; a reviewer may want to confirm GEM's intended milestone. Independent corroboration (Argus: 'Phase I completed September 2013') seen in research but not verifiable (bot-blocked).

Golden Pass import/regas terminal (Sabine Pass, TX; QatarEnergy/ExxonMobil) went idle in 2011. S&P Global (via Wayback snapshot of the 5-Feb-2019 FID article) states verbatim: 'US Department of Energy data show Golden Pass has not imported any gas since June 2011.' Corroborated by the primary EIA import series ('Golden Pass, TX LNG Imports from Qatar', data begins 2011). Terminal imported briefly 2010-2011 (first cargo Oct 2010) then sat idle amid the US shale glut before its 2019 FID export conversion. 2011 = last import / start of the idle-mothball period. Two independent origins (S&P reporting + EIA/DOE primary data).

Harvest Midway Terminal (crude storage/pumping hub at Taft, TX, feeding the Ingleside export terminals near Corpus Christi) was announced Nov 2019 with the Midway Terminal projected in-service at the start of 4Q 2020. Harvest's own history page states 'In 2020, Harvest completed the Ingleside Pipeline... transports products from our Midway Terminal.' Year = 2020. Both verified URLs are Harvest's own (one origin) -> single primary source, tier medium; no independent media source confirming the 2020 in-service date was verifiable before the session web limit.

Houston Fuel Oil Terminal Company (HFOTCO), Houston Ship Channel, was founded in 1978, originally dedicated to storing/blending/moving residual fuel oil (added crude oil handling in the early 1990s). Year = 1978 (founding used as operating-start proxy). One industry source (TankTerminals) verified PASS for '1978'+'Houston Fuel Oil Terminal'; RBN Energy independently states 'Founded in 1978' but was bot-blocked (403) and could not be verified. Tier medium pending a second verifiable source.

1922 = year marine petroleum-terminal operations began at the St. Rose site (former Cedar Grove Plantation / Carson site). St. Charles Parish history timeline states verbatim: '1922 - Cities Service Oil Company begins operating in St. Rose at Carson site.' IMTT (company founded 1939) later took over the existing oil-export terminal. Two independent publishers verified via Wayback (live pages 403 bot-block the verifier): St. Charles Parish Virtual History Museum (scphistory.org) and the official St. Charles Parish government site (stcharlesparish.gov). CAVEAT: an even earlier operation, Carson Petroleum, began at the same site in 1919 (also on the scphistory timeline), but all sources anchor the terminal that became IMTT to the 1922 Cities Service oil-export terminal, so 1922 is the defensible operating-start; the modern IMTT St. Rose complex has been continuously expanded since.

The proposal to convert the Kenai LNG terminal (Nikiski, AK) into an LNG import facility ('Kenai LNG Cool Down Project') was filed with FERC on March 29, 2019 by Marathon subsidiary Trans-Foreland Pipeline Co. (docket CP19-118); FERC issued its environmental-review schedule notice June 2019 and approved the project Dec 17, 2020. Year proposed = 2019. Primary/regulatory source (Federal Register, June 2019 notice) + independent media (Petroleum News) both verified PASS for '2019'+'Kenai'.

Seabrook Logistics LLC (Magellan Midstream/LBC 50-50 JV) crude-oil and condensate marine terminal near Seabrook, TX (Galveston Bay). The Dec-2016 Magellan/LBC joint announcement states the new storage and pipeline infrastructure was expected to be operational in the first quarter of 2017. Year = 2017 (announced/projected commercial start). Only the Magellan/LBC press release (one origin; reprints are the same wire story) verified PASS for '2017'+'Seabrook'; tier medium. CAVEAT: 2017 is the projected start from the Dec-2016 release; no independent post-startup confirmation of the actual 2017 in-service date was verifiable before the session web limit.

Lake Charles LNG export project (BG Group + Energy Transfer) publicly announced/proposed October 1, 2013 via a project development agreement to convert the existing Trunkline import terminal into a 3-train liquefaction/export facility (T1-T3). FEED and FERC pre-filing had been under way since mid-2012, but the public proposal of the export project dates to 2013. Two independent sources (Eversheds LNG Law Blog Oct 2013; NGI FERC-filing article).

Lake Charles / Trunkline LNG import-regas terminal mothballed 2012. Argus (Dec 2025 'Lake Charles cancellation shifts tide' article) states verbatim: 'Its Lake Charles regasification terminal, mothballed since 2012, was prime real estate...'. Verifier PASS for 2012+Lake Charles. Context corroborates (EIA: at least 5 US LNG import terminals imported nothing in 2012 amid the shale glut), and Wikipedia repeats 'mothballed since 2012' but I could not get a 2nd DISTINCT verifiable page whose 2012 clearly ties to the mothball milestone (NS Energy 403; Wikipedia snapshot did not surface the string to the verifier). Single strong trade-press source -> tier medium.

Woodside took the Final Investment Decision on the foundational phase of Louisiana LNG (Calcasieu Parish, LA; 3-train, 16.5 Mtpa) on 29 April 2025. Project formerly known as Driftwood LNG, acquired by Woodside via its 2024 Tellurian acquisition. FID year confirmed by Woodside's own media release (sponsor/primary) and independent trade press (LNG Prime); NS Energy project page (Wayback) corroborates. Two+ independent sources, year explicit.

This is the Mt. Airy, LA marine terminal (St. John the Baptist Parish), which physically began operating when Pin Oak Terminals opened it on 16-17 August 2017 (Phase 1; construction from late 2015). MPLX acquired the asset from Pin Oak Holdings in September 2018 — so the terminal's operating-start = 2017, while MPLX ownership dates from 2018. GEM appears to track the same physical asset under both 'MPLX Mount Airy Terminal' and 'Pin Oak Terminal'. If GEM intends operating-under-MPLX, that would be 2018; commissioning of the terminal itself = 2017. Year 2017 confirmed by Mercuria (lead investor/primary) and Louisiana Economic Development (state).

Magnolia LNG (Lake Charles, LA; subsidiary of Australia's Liquefied Natural Gas Ltd / LNGL) was publicly proposed in 2013, announced by Gov. Bobby Jindal and Magnolia LNG as a $2.2bn export facility at the Port of Lake Charles. The Lake Charles site was leased in Dec 2012, with the public project announcement in 2013. Year confirmed by Louisiana Economic Development (state/primary announcement) and independent maritime press (gCaptain).

Enterprise Products Partners' Morgan's Point ethane export terminal (Houston Ship Channel / La Porte, TX) began service in 2016 — commissioning/startup July 2016, first export cargo (M/V JS INEOS Intrepid, ~265,000 bbl to INEOS Rafnes, Norway) loaded September 2016. Commercial-operations year = 2016, confirmed by three independent publishers (Argus, Tanks & Terminals, Construction Boxscore).

LPG export from Sunoco Logistics' (now Energy Transfer) Nederland, TX terminal began via the Mariner South project; the first propane export cargo loaded out of Nederland in February 2015 (S&P Global Platts, 17 Feb 2015 — bot-blocked, no Wayback snapshot available, so not stagable). Only one independently accessible source verified (Butane-Propane News / bpnews, non-primary trade), hence tier low. The Nederland marine terminal itself is decades older (Sun Oil era); 2015 reflects the LPG-export operating start, which is the gas-relevant milestone.

2012 = year NuStar's Corpus Christi crude liquids storage terminal (i.e. the North Beach terminal) became operational. Offshore-technology/GlobalData OT Market Data page (Wayback snapshot) states verbatim: 'NuStar Energy operates the Corpus Christi Crude liquids storage terminal... This liquids storage terminal became operational in 2012.' Verifier PASS for 2012+NuStar. Corroborating context (independent, but not a discrete milestone statement so kept at medium): NuStar's South Texas Crude Oil Pipeline reached the 'existing' 1.6-million-bbl North Beach terminal delivering Eagle Ford crude, and NGI (9 Nov 2012) already treats the North Beach crude terminal as operating. CAVEAT: the OT page names it 'Corpus Christi Crude liquids storage terminal' (does NOT use the literal 'North Beach' name), though it is NuStar's Corpus Christi crude storage terminal; the Sept-2013 dock, the 10-Apr-2014 third dock, and the Dec-2016 Martin-Midstream-acquired adjacent docks are later expansion milestones, not first operations.

NuStar's St. James (LA) crude/products storage terminal became operational in 2006 per Offshore-technology market data (sole verifiable source, an aggregator, fetched via Wayback because the live page is bot-blocked). NuStar is a 2007 spin-off of Valero's midstream assets; St. James was built out in phases (the cited 'St. James IV' implies later phase expansions) from ~2006. Single non-primary source, so tier low; could not independently corroborate the 2006 date.

The Phillips 66 Beaumont Terminal (Gulf Coast crude/products terminal in the Beaumont/Nederland, TX area) was originally established by Smith Bluff Pure Oil Co. on 5 April 1923; Phillips 66 held a centennial celebration on 5 April 2023 ('100 years to the day'). The terminal passed Pure Oil -> Unocal (1960s) -> Chevron (1990s) -> Phillips 66 (acquired June 2014). 'Began operating'/commissioning = 1923; if GEM intends the current-owner start, that would be 2014. One verified non-primary source (Port Arthur News) for the 1923 founding (the trerc.tamu.edu corroborating article is bot-blocked with no Wayback snapshot), hence tier low.

Pin Oak Terminals' multi-product liquid marine terminal at Mt. Airy, LA (St. John the Baptist Parish, Mississippi River) opened 16-17 August 2017 (Phase 1; construction began late 2015 after Mercuria's Dec 2016 investment). Operating-start = 2017, confirmed by Mercuria (key investor/primary) and Louisiana Economic Development (state). NB: this is the same physical asset later sold to MPLX in Sept 2018 (see GEM 'MPLX Mount Airy Terminal' record) — GEM appears to carry it twice.

Plains All American began building its St. James (LA) crude terminal in 2004; the initial ~3.5 MMbbl storage phase became operational in Q1 2007 (RBN Energy, fetched via Wayback because the live page is bot-blocked). Subsequent expansions followed (Mississippi River dock 2009, rail receipt 2010, +1.2 MMbbl 2012). Operating-start = 2007. Single non-primary analyst source verified (OGJ's 2004 planning article and the Plains/BusinessWire releases are bot-blocked with no Wayback snapshots), hence tier low.

Year SPOT was first publicly proposed via its federal Deepwater Port Act license application (Enterprise Products' offshore crude-oil export terminal ~27-31 nm off Brazoria County, TX). MARAD/USCG received the application 31 Jan 2019; Federal Register Notice of Application published 4 Mar 2019. Three independent sources confirm 2019 (regulatory FR notice + Offshore Magazine + Oil & Gas Journal). NOTE: SPOT is a CRUDE OIL export terminal, not an LNG terminal.

CRUDE OIL terminal (Seaway Crude Pipeline Co., Enterprise/Enbridge 50/50 JV), not LNG. 2012 = crude began arriving at the Freeport-area terminus on 6 Jun 2012 after the Seaway pipeline reversal, the documented operational milestone specific to Freeport in its modern crude-receipt/storage role. AMBIGUOUS: the original Seaway system became operational 23 Nov 1976 with Freeport as the southern terminus, so the facility predates 2012; no terminal-specific commissioning date is separately documented. Single non-GEM source (Wikipedia) verified for 2012+Freeport; low tier.

CRUDE OIL terminal (Seaway Crude Pipeline Co., Enterprise/Enbridge JV), not LNG. 1976 = the original Seaway system became operational 23 Nov 1976; the original pipeline explicitly included the terminal and distribution network at Texas City, TX. Flow was reversed in 2012, but the Texas City terminal itself dates to the original 1976 system. Single non-GEM source (Wikipedia) verified for 1976+Texas City; exact terminal commissioning date not separately documented; low tier.

CRUDE OIL export terminal at Ingleside, Port of Corpus Christi (originally Buckeye/Phillips 66/Marathon JV; now Gibson Energy), not LNG. Began operations 16 Jul 2020 (first marine vessel loaded; in-service). GlobeNewswire (Buckeye press release) and the PGJ reprint both trace to the same 16 Jul 2020 Buckeye announcement (one source); Gibson Energy's current operations page is an independent corroboration of the 2020 start, so >=2 independent sources confirm 2020. High tier.

'South Texas LNG Terminal' (2-train, FID substatus 'planned') corresponds to Glenfarne Group's Texas LNG export terminal at the Port of Brownsville, TX (2 trains, 4 MTPA). FID is PLANNED/EXPECTED, not yet taken: as of Feb 2026 the project remained on schedule for a Q2 2026 final investment decision, and no formal FID announcement was found as of late Jun 2026 (consistent with GEM substatus 'planned'). Two independent sources (Pipeline & Gas Journal + offshore-energy.biz) verify the 2026 target. CAVEAT: this is a projected FID year that previously slipped from end-2025/early-2026 and could move again; tier kept at medium because the milestone is unrealized rather than a documented historical event.

CRUDE OIL export deepwater port ~26.6 nm off Brazoria County, TX (Sentinel Midstream / Texas GulfLink LLC), not LNG. 2019 = first publicly proposed via its federal Deepwater Port Act license application; MARAD/USCG received the application 30 May 2019 and published the Federal Register Notice of Application 26 Jun 2019. Regulatory FR notice + Oil & Gas Journal (two independent origins) confirm 2019.

No independent non-circular source documents a specific 4-digit operating-start year for this marine terminal or the Valero Corpus Christi East refinery's marine operations. Lineage is well established (CLUI, TSHA, company histories): the East Plant is a ~115,000 bpd refinery 'built in the 1960s' that Valero acquired in 2001; traces to the Sinclair Oil Corpus Christi refinery bought by Coastal (Oscar Wyatt) in the 'early 1960s', then Coastal -> El Paso -> Valero (2001). Every credible source gives only a DECADE ('1960s'/'early 1960s'), never a 4-digit year, and none ties a year to the marine-terminal/dock operations-start milestone; 2001 is only Valero's acquisition. Genuinely pre-documentation; UNRESOLVED per the no-weak-year rule.

CRUDE/refined-products marine terminal at Valero's West (Bill Greehey) Corpus Christi refinery, not LNG. 1984 = year refining operations commenced at the grass-roots West plant (Valero commissioned the refinery in 1983; commercial refining began 1984). CAVEAT: the cited pages document the REFINERY's start, used here as a proxy for the co-located marine terminal because no terminal-specific commissioning date is documented; Valero's own locations page states 1983 commissioning. Low tier (proxy + minor 1983/1984 conflict).

terminal: West Delta LNG Deepwater Port Terminal
researcher_notes: LNG export deepwater port ~10.5 nm off Plaquemines Parish, LA (LNG 21 / West Delta LNG LLC; 6 modular trains, 6.1 MTPA). 2019 = first publicly proposed via its federal Deepwater Port Act license application; MARAD/USCG received the application 28 Aug 2019 and published the Federal Register Notice of Application 4 Oct 2019. Regulatory FR notice + Natural Gas Intelligence + 1012 Industry Report (+ the developer's own site) confirm 2019. (Application later terminated by MARAD in 2025, leaving the project shelved.)

No externally-verifiable shelving year exists. This is a GEM-inferred status ('shelved, inferred 2 y'): no sponsor announced a pause. The Sycar FLNG (at the Complejo Petroquimico Jose Antonio Anzoategui, near Barcelona, Anzoategui) was proposed Nov 2022 via a Sycar-PDVSA MoU (signed 10-11 Nov 2022; LNG Prime, Riviera, Petroleumag/GNLglobal [es]), targeting first LNG exports 'as early as 2024'. It went dormant after the US OFAC license route closed -- OFAC General License 44 expired 18 Apr 2024 and Venezuela oil/gas sanctions were restored -- which foreclosed the project's required US export licence. Per GEM lifecycle rules an 'inferred 2 y' year = the year the 2-year-dormancy inference was made (i.e. Nov 2022 + 2y, ~2024) -- an internal GEM value, not an event reported by any independent publisher, so it cannot be corroborated by the URL verifier (no page ties this terminal to a shelving YEAR). Documented anchor: proposal Nov 2022. Suggested fill if methodology is applied directly: 2024 (or the actual year-of-inference). Marked UNRESOLVED because the shelved-milestone year is unsourceable by design. Spanish-language searches (gnlglobal.com, petroleumag.com) found only the 2022 proposal, no shelving announcement.

GEM ties the Ca Mau LNG Terminal (sponsor PetroVietnam Power) to the Ca Mau 3 LNG-to-power project. The verified source (Vietnam Energy magazine, published 02 July 2020) shows the Ca Mau 3 LNG combined-cycle project being readied for submission/approval into the national Power Development Plan in mid-2020 (operation targeted 2026-2027). CAVEAT/why low tier: this article describes the associated LNG-to-power PLANT, not an import terminal explicitly, and only one URL passed the verifier (power-technology.com Ca Mau 3 profile 403'd). 2020 is the best-supported proposal year for the Ca Mau LNG-to-power project the terminal belongs to.

Cai Mep LNG terminal (Hai Linh Co., Cai Mep Industrial Zone, Ba Ria-Vung Tau) construction began in 2018 (Q2 2018). GAS SOUTH (pgs.com.vn, a PV Gas subsidiary trade page) states construction of the Hai Linh terminal 'commenced in the second quarter of 2018'; the Vietnamese energy journal nangluongvietnam.vn corroborates a Q2/2018 construction start ('Dự kiến dự án khởi công xây dựng quý 2/2018'). Consistent with physical evidence: S&P Global (Jun 2020) reported construction essentially completed and a test run expected late 2020; storage-tank contract awarded to Lilama 18. Tier=medium/independent=false because one corroborating source frames Q2-2018 as a projection rather than a confirmed ground-breaking, so the two are not fully independent contemporary confirmations - but both point to 2018 and it fits the completed-by-2020 timeline. CAUTION: distinct from the PV Gas 'Thi Vai LNG terminal' (broke ground 28 Oct 2019) at the same Cai Mep-Thi Vai port complex - do not conflate.

This is a GEM-INFERRED cancellation (substatus 'inferred 4 y'), not a publicly announced one. ExxonMobil + Hai Phong People's Committee + JERA signed an MOU for a Hai Phong LNG-to-power project in 2020; the project then went silent and was excluded from Power Development Plan 8 (approved May 2023). No independent source states a year in which the Cat Hai/Hai Phong FSRU was 'cancelled' - the cancellation is an inference from prolonged inactivity (~4 years of no updates as of Aug 2025). Because no page ties the terminal to a specific cancellation YEAR, leaving UNRESOLVED rather than cite a date no source asserts.

This Haiphong FSRU is the Vingroup/VinEnergo Hai Phong LNG-to-power project (distinct from the cancelled Cat Hai/Exxon-JERA FSRU). It was first publicly proposed/announced in 2025: Vingroup and VinEnergo formed their JV (LNG Prime, 12 June 2025), the project received its investment registration certificate on 23 June 2025, and ground was broken in Sept 2025. Two independent publishers (LNG Prime; The Investor) both verified with 2025 + Vingroup.

Long An LNG-to-power was first proposed via the GS Energy-VinaCapital MoU signed in November 2019; LNG Prime (Nov 2019) verified with 2019 + Long An. The 2019 MoU is widely reported, but only this one URL passed the verifier this run - nsenergybusiness (403) and the Nasdaq 2021 reprint (404) failed - so single-source low tier. Project later licensed/IRC March 2021 and KEXIM financing MoU June 2023, but the FIRST proposal milestone is the Nov 2019 MoU.

Long Son LNG Power Complex (Ba Ria-Vung Tau): Phase 1 was supplemented into Vietnam's national power master plan by the PM on 23 April 2020, and GE signed an MoU with EVNGENCO3 to develop it in November 2020 - so 2020 is the proposal year. world-energy.org ('GE Makes Deal for Vietnam LNG Project', Nov 2020) verified with 2020 + Long Son. Single-source low tier: rigzone (HTTP 202), nsenergybusiness (403), aseanenergy (404) and genco3 (timeout) all failed verification this run.

Energy Capital Vietnam's (ECV) Mui Ke Ga LNG-to-power + FSRU project was publicly proposed in 2020: the PM directed it be added to the National Power Development Plan (directive 23 July 2020, announced 13 Aug 2020). Verified by two different publishers with 2020 + Mui Ke Ga: ECV's PR Newswire release and Vietnam Investment Review's independent coverage of the same PM directive. (Note: one source is ECV's own release and the other is VIR reporting the government action - treated as independent publishers rather than a primary+own-echo.)

GEM's 'Nam Dinh LNG Terminal' is the JAPEX/ITECO Northern Vietnam LNG terminal (at Nam Dinh Vu Industrial Park, Hai Phong). It was publicly proposed/announced in 2022: JAPEX announced its participation on 11 January 2022 (after a Dec 2021 share-purchase agreement with ITECO), with FID targeted for 2H 2022. Verified across three independent sources (JAPEX corporate release [primary], Natural Gas World, LNG Prime), all containing 2022.

Quynh Lap was a coal project (Quynh Lap I & II, 2,400 MW) under PDP VII; it was converted to an LNG-to-power project (1,500 MW) in Power Development Plan 8, approved 15 May 2023 (Decision 500/QD-TTg) - which is the year it was first established/proposed as an LNG project. Verified by the PDP8 plan document itself [primary/regulatory] plus Watson Farley & Williams and Vietnam Investment Review, all with 2023 + Quynh Lap. NUANCE: a July-2022 PDP8 draft had also listed it as LNG, so an argument exists for 2022; 2023 (formal PDP8 approval) is the better-sourced and official milestone.

Son My LNG terminal (Binh Thuan) first publicly proposed in 2017: AES and PetroVietnam Gas (PV Gas) signed an MOU on 12 November 2017, witnessed by Presidents Trump and Tran Dai Quang during Trump's state visit to Vietnam, to jointly develop the Son My LNG terminal. Confirmed by contemporary independent media (Vietnam Investment Review / vir.com.vn, dated 20 Nov 2017, reporting the MOU 'inked with AES Corporation on November 12') and by AES Vietnam's own press release ('In November 2017, AES signed an MOU with PV Gas... to develop the... Son My LNG Terminal Project'). Independent origins (media + sponsor). Verifier confirms '2017'+'Son My' present on both.

Son My is a multi-phase project: Phase 1 = 3.6 MTPA, Phase 2 = 6 MTPA. The 6 MTPA Phase 2 was explicitly enumerated when the project received Binh Thuan investment-policy approval on 11 Jul 2023 (both verified sources are 2023). LOW-CONFIDENCE / milestone caveat: the multi-phase concept (3.6/6/10 MTPA) dates to PV Gas's 2015 feasibility study and the project's ~Oct 2019 government approval, so the true 'first publicly proposed' year of the Phase 2 expansion may be ~2015-2019. 2023 is the verifiable point at which Phase 2 = 6 MTPA was formally defined in the sanctioned project; reviewer should confirm whether GEM's Phase 2 'proposed' milestone is the original-plan year or the 2023 sanction. Web-search budget (session limit) was exhausted before an earlier year could be independently verified.

Thi Vai Phase 2 = expansion of the existing 1 MTPA terminal to 3 MTPA. Petrovietnam formally directed PV Gas to triple capacity to 3 MTPA at a 3 Feb 2025 working session, with PV Gas ready to sign the EPC contract in late 2025 (both verified sources are Feb 2025, independent publishers). LOW-CONFIDENCE / milestone caveat: the 3 MTPA second phase already appeared in the project's original phased design (Phase 1 = 1 MTPA ops ~2023, Phase 2 = 3 MTPA), so the 'first publicly proposed' year may be ~2019-2021. 2025 is the verifiable formal expansion proposal; reviewer should confirm whether GEM's Phase 2 'proposed' milestone is the original-plan year or the 2025 directive. Web-search budget (session limit) was exhausted before an earlier year could be independently verified.

The Tien Lang FSRU was part of ExxonMobil's ~$5.09bn Tien Lang 1 IP LNG-to-power complex (Haiphong 1, 4,500 MW). Cancellation is GEM-inferred (substatus 'inferred 4 y'). Best-documented abandonment event: the Tien Lang / Haiphong LNG-power projects were dropped from the draft Power Development Plan 8 submitted 21 Feb 2022 (verified source, The Investor, 19 Mar 2022). The project was not in final PDP8 (approved May 2023); offshore-technology (Oct 2021) still listed it as merely proposed, and there is no later activity. Staged 2022 = year removed from the national power plan = de facto cancellation. Single independent media source (no primary/regulatory filing accessible), hence tier low; the 2022 value itself is well-supported.
